title: Tor comparison from a chart to its sharp face localization
statement:
Let $P$ be a fine saturated commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], let $A$ be a strictly henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and let $\alpha:P\to A$ be the structural map of a chart of an fs log structure $M$ on $\operatorname{Spec}A$, taken at the closed geometric point, with log stalk $M_{\bar x}$ there. Put $F=\{p\in P\mid \alpha(p)\in A^\times\}$, $P_F=\{p-f:p\in P,f\in F\}\subset P^{\rm gp}$, and $P_x=P_F/F^{\rm gp}$. Choose a monoid section $s:P_x\to P_F$ of the quotient and a sharp characteristic chart [lem-trf-log-regular-sharp-chart] $b:P_x\to A$ of the same log structure, i.e. the structural map of a chart $b_M:P_x\to M_{\bar x}$ whose induced identification $P_x\cong\overline M_{\bar x}$ is the one induced by $\alpha$. Then there is a monoid homomorphism $u:P_x\to A^\times$ with $\alpha(s(q))=u(q)b(q)$ for every $q$. For every monoid ideal $H\subset P$, if $H_x$ is its image in $P_x$, the face localization $\mathbf Z[P]\to\mathbf Z[P_F]$, the splitting $P_F\cong P_x\oplus F^{\rm gp}$, the unit twist $z^q\mapsto u(q)z^q$ on $A[P_x]$ (after extension of coefficients from $\mathbf Z$ to $A$), and the resulting change of rings induce a natural isomorphism of Tor groups [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], where $A$ is a $\mathbf Z[P]$-algebra by $z^p\mapsto\alpha(p)$ on the left and a $\mathbf Z[P_x]$-algebra by $z^q\mapsto b(q)$ on the right:
$$\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathbf Z[P]}_1(\mathbf Z[P]/\mathbf Z[H],A)\;\cong\;\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathbf Z[P_x]}_1(\mathbf Z[P_x]/\mathbf Z[H_x],A).$$

source.place: Expose VI, 3.7(a), printed p. 75 (face localization, splitting and unit pushout), together with Expose VIII, proof of Lemma 3.4.3, printed p. 110 (the induced monomial Tor comparison).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-chart-face-split-coordinates] to the given log stalk and its two charts. It supplies $\alpha_F$, $Q=P_x$, $G=F^{\rm gp}$, $P_F\simeq Q\oplus G$, $c=\alpha_Fs$, $v=\alpha_F|_G$ and $u$ with $c=ub$. It also supplies $H_x\subset Q$ as an ideal and $H_F=H_x\oplus G$. Its chart-pushout hypothesis is exactly the definition of the two given charts; no log-regularity hypothesis is needed. Its integrality hypothesis on $M=M_{\bar x}$ holds by [lem-per-integral-monoid-unit-pushout] with its submonoid $E=F$, its group $A^\times$ and $f=\alpha|_F$: $P$ is integral (fine), and $M\cong P\oplus_FA^\times$ by the chart, so $M$ is cancellative and embeds in its group completion.

source.place: Expose VI 1.1--1.2 (printed p. 69), 3.7(a) (printed p. 75); Expose VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5 (printed pp. 98--99). Agent algebraic expansion of chart pushouts and the given section; returned parent steps 1, 2, 4.

proof.text: For the given $H$, apply [lem-trf-monoid-face-localization-ideal-tensor] with $P,F,A,\alpha$. Its hypothesis holds since $F=\alpha^{-1}(A^\times)$. Obtain the multiplication-compatible $A$-linear isomorphism $\lambda$ from $\mathbf Z[H]\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}A$ to $\mathbf Z[H_F]\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P_F]}A$.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.2 (printed p. 98) and proof of 3.4.3 (printed p. 110). Agent algebraic localization calculation on monomial ideal tensors; returned parent step 5 and monomial-basis clause of step 4.

proof.text: In the splitting from step 1, apply [lem-trf-split-unit-group-ideal-tensor] with $K=H_x$, group $G$, and characters $c,v$. The coefficient action is $\alpha_F(s(q)+g)=c(q)v(g)$. Obtain $\sigma$ from the last tensor to $\mathbf Z[H_x]\otimes_{\mathbf Z[Q]}A_c$; its inverse is the change-of-rings ideal-tensor map for $\mathbf Z[Q]\to\mathbf Z[P_F]$.

source.place: Expose VI 3.7(a) (printed p. 75), with the chart-tensor setting of Expose VIII proof of 3.4.3 (printed p. 110). Agent split group-factor calculation; returned parent step 6.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-monoid-unit-twist-ideal-tensor] with $K=H_x$ and $c=ub$. It supplies $\rho$ to $\mathbf Z[H_x]\otimes_{\mathbf Z[Q]}A_b$ and identifies it with the unit twist over $A[Q]$ using the coefficient-extension isomorphisms, which require no flatness. Hence $\theta=\rho\sigma\lambda$ is an isomorphism commuting with multiplication to $A$.

source.place: Expose VI 3.7(a) (printed p. 75) and Expose VIII proof of 3.4.3 (printed p. 110). Agent unit-character and coefficient-extension calculation; returned parent step 7.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-tor-symmetry] and part (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-tor-ideal-kernel-naturality], the two first Tor groups are the kernels of the two multiplication maps. Restrict $\theta$ to obtain their isomorphism. Part (b) identifies its factors with change of rings: localization goes forward, the split inclusion goes backward, and coefficient extension and the twist go forward. The naturality clauses of steps 1--4 and the boundary identity in part (b) prove naturality for compatible coefficient data; $s,b$ remain fixed. On $p=s(\bar p)+g$ its ideal-tensor formula is $z^p\otimes a\mapsto z^{\bar p}\otimes v(g)u(\bar p)a$, so it is the stipulated comparison.
